citation: Heller, J. I., Daehler, K. R., Wong, N., Shinohara, M., & Miratrix, L. W. (2012). Differential effects of three professional development models on teacher knowledge and student achievement in elementary science. Journal of Research in Science Teaching, 49(3), 333-362. https://doi.org/10.1002/tea.21004
report_number: JRST 49(3):333-362; DOI 10.1002/tea.21004; ERIC EJ989348. NSF Teacher Professional Continuum Program, grant 0545445. WestEd 'Making Sense of SCIENCE' / Learning Science for Teaching RCT.
design: Cluster RCT (counterbalanced, two rounds, with a delayed/follow-up year). Unit of assignment = Teacher/Class: teachers randomly assigned within site (within-school where >=2 participants; otherwise blocked on prior school-level state test scores) to one of three PD courses or a no-treatment control. 446 teachers randomized (324 intervention, 122 control; Table 3); 271 retained, 253 provided student data; ~7,000 grade-4 students (intact classes, not randomized). 8 research sites in 6 states (AZ, 2xCA, WA, MA, 2xNC, AL). Subject = elementary science (electric circuits). Three TPD arms sharing an identical science-content component, differing in pedagogy-analysis: A=Teaching Cases, B=Looking at Student Work, C=Metacognitive Analysis (= 'Content Immersion' in the 2010 SREE version). NOTE: registry row 46 codes grade 7-12 / Average-High SES, but the study is unambiguously grade 4 elementary science -- the registry grade/SES appears miscoded.
problems:
DUPLICATE STUDY -- registry row 46 ('Heller 2012') == registry row 45 ('Heller et al. 2010'). They are the SAME randomized trial: row 45 was extracted from the 2010 SREE conference paper (ERIC ED514193) and row 46 is the peer-reviewed journal version (this JRST 49(3):333-362 article). The central merge should DROP ONE of these two registry rows to avoid double-counting; recommend keeping the journal version (row 46, this file) over the conference abstract (row 45). Both report the same student-achievement contrasts (three science-PD arms vs one shared no-treatment control). The published student content-knowledge study-year effect sizes differ slightly between versions (2012 JRST Table 4: 0.37 / 0.57 / 0.60 for Teaching Cases / Looking at Student Work / Metacognitive Analysis; 2010 SREE: 0.39 / 0.52 / 0.52) -- the journal values are the more refined/final published estimates.

WHAT THIS PDF DOES AND DOES NOT CONTAIN: the journal article reports student effect sizes directly in Table 4 (p.351) but the detailed HLM impact coefficients, standard errors, standardizing SDs, and per-condition student sample sizes are in the online Supporting Information (Tables S19-S21 plus an Unadjusted Results Supplement), which are NOT in this PDF. Consequences: (1) impact_estimate / impact_se / mean_t / sd_t / mean_c / sd_c are left null because they are not in the main article (the text gives only that intervention students gained ~19-22 pct pts vs ~13 pct pts for controls; Question 3, p.352). (2) The reported ES (Table 4) are the authors' standardized mean differences (HLM treatment coefficient / pooled SD of student gain), taken here as d, with Hedges' small-sample correction J applied to obtain g. (3) Because the cluster-adjusted SE is not available in this PDF, g_var/g_se are computed with the student-level large-sample SMD variance formula and are NOT cluster-adjusted (cluster_adjusted=false); the cluster correction should be applied centrally (Hedges 2007), but the design-effect ICC is NOT reported in this article (do not guess). (4) Per-condition student n are NOT in this PDF; the n_t/n_c values recorded are borrowed from the 2010 SREE companion analytic gain-score samples (A=1347, B=1392, C=1013, control=1494) for the SAME trial, used only to set df/J and the approximate g_var -- flagged as cross-version borrow; the journal abstract states 'over 7,000 students' total and 253 teachers provided student data.

TEST TYPE: the student outcome is a 34-item developer-made electric-circuits content test (selected-response percent-correct; Cronbach alpha 0.87), validated by the developers but NOT an independent/standardized instrument -- so the meta-analysis (independent measures only) would likely filter these out; extracted and labeled test_type=researcher_made per spec.

TIMEPOINT: extracted the immediate post (study-year) wave (pretest-to-posttest gain within 2 weeks of completing the unit, 2007-08). A follow-up-year wave also exists (next cohort of the same teachers' students; Table 4 ES 0.48/0.50/0.75) but is a different student cohort, not the immediate post-intervention sample, so not extracted as the primary contrast.

ALL THREE ARMS SHARE THE SAME no-treatment control, so the three effect sizes are not independent; central merge should pick one arm or average to avoid double-counting the control.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Teaching Cases (science PD) vs no-treatment control
effect_sizes.test_name: Student electric-circuits science content test (34 items, selected-response percent correct; developer-made, Cronbach alpha 0.87), pretest-to-posttest gain
effect_sizes.timepoint: post, study year (gain post minus pre, within 2 weeks after the electric circuits unit, 2007-08)
effect_sizes.g_method: Author-reported ES from Table 4 (p.351) = 0.37 taken as d (= HLM treatment coefficient / pooled SD of student gain; the standardizing SD and HLM coefficient/SE are in Supporting Info Tables S20, not in this PDF). Hedges' g = J*d, df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2839, J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) = 0.999736, g = 0.36990. g_var via student-level SMD formula Var(d) = (n_t+n_c)/(n_t*n_c) + d^2/(2*(n_t+n_c)) = 0.001436, g_var = J^2*Var(d) = 0.001435, g_se = 0.03788. NOT cluster-adjusted (cluster SE unavailable in this PDF); apply Hedges 2007 cluster correction centrally, but no design ICC is reported. n_t/n_c borrowed from the 2010 SREE companion (same trial) since per-arm n is not in this article.
